sections.heading: C — Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals
sections.markdown:
## C — Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Solid white fog lines mark the right edge of the road and help you stay on it at night or in bad weather, and crossing them to pass is illegal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Solid white lines also separate same-direction lanes where lane changes are risky, such as sharp curves and freeway acceleration and deceleration lanes, and you should not cross them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
A double solid white line separates two same-direction travel paths, and crossing it is prohibited. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Crosswalks are marked by solid white lines painted across the pavement or by white stripes laid in the direction of traffic, at intersections and sometimes midblock. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Stop behind the crosswalk line. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
A stop line is a wide white line across a lane showing where to stop at an intersection, keeping you clear of pedestrians and cross traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
With no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection, and in every case make sure you can see traffic from all directions before going. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A02
Wide white arrows down the middle of a lane show the movements allowed from it; in the handbook example the far-right lane is right turn only, the next lane allows right or straight, and turning right from the other two lanes is illegal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A02
A bicycle lane, shown by special markings and signs, is reserved only for bicyclists. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A02
Green paint in a bike lane flags a likely conflict point between cars and bicycles, usually at intersections and driveways, so take extra care turning there. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A02
Driving, passing, turning right, parking, pulling over to wait, or making a delivery in a bike lane is illegal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A02
Shared lane markings show proper lane position and traffic flow, and when you see one, watch for bicyclists and give them room as legal road users. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A02
Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and come as solid, broken and center-lane lines. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A02
A single broken yellow center line on a two-way road usually means you may pass when it is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A02
Do not cross a solid yellow line on your side of the center line to pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
On a four-lane divided road or a one-way road, a solid yellow line usually marks the pavement's left edge. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
A double solid yellow center line on a two-lane road bans passing in both directions, though you may cross it to turn into a driveway or crossroad or reach a parking spot. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A03
A left-turn-only center lane has solid yellow lines on its outer edges and broken yellow lines inside, and left turns may be made from it in either direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A03
Using the left-turn-only center lane to pass or merge is illegal and dangerous. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A03
Michigan Lefts, or indirect left turns, have been used since the late 1960s; where they exist you cannot turn left directly but drive straight or turn right and then U-turn at a median crossover. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A03
A single-lane Michigan Left crossover takes one vehicle at a time; extra width is there for tractor trailers and RVs that need a wider turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A03
A multi-lane Michigan Left lets two vehicles turn together when arrows, ONLY lettering and solid white lines show it, and an unmarked crossover is always treated as single-lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A03
From the main highway, drive past the intersection, turn left into the median crossover, then turn left back onto the main highway when clear, and then either keep going straight or get into the far-right lane to make a right onto the cross road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A03
From the cross road, turn right onto the main highway, move to the far-left lane, turn left into the median crossover, and when clear turn left onto the main highway and continue straight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A04
Yield lines appear at roundabouts and midblock crosswalks, and when yielding you stop behind them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A04
White triangles painted across a lane mean be ready to stop and yield to pedestrians. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A04
Dashed white lines across a lane in a roundabout mark the edge of its circular lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A04
Driving through a store parking lot or any other public or private property to get around a traffic-control device is illegal. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A04
A red light, at the top of Michigan signals, means stop behind the crosswalk or stop line. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A04
A yellow light means the signal is about to turn red, and you are required to stop; when a safe stop is impossible, do not accelerate, and go through the intersection with caution. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A04
A green light means proceed with caution after checking for pedestrians and vehicles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A04
If a signal is not working and no officer or other device controls traffic, stop completely, yield to vehicles already there, and yield to the right on a tie. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A04
The 5-section-head or doghouse signal controls turns with red, yellow and green lights plus a yellow and a green turn arrow. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A04
A lit green arrow on a doghouse signal gives a protected turn with conflicting traffic stopped, while the green light lets you turn only after oncoming traffic clears. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]

items.why: The handbook teaches Michigan Lefts and lane markings through route diagrams, and following a multi-step turn path or matching a line pattern is spatial reading that a text flashcard cannot train; a diagram-based drill is needed.
